Dr Susan Clayton
Endocrinologist
Women’s Health Center
11-13 Bell Street
Newtown

28/03/2014

Dear Dr Clayton,

Re: Ms Tracy Browen,                               DOB 22/07/1988                                           Comment [Benchmark1]: Bowen




I am writing to refer Ms Browen, a 26-year-old female married patient, whose clinical features are          Comment [Benchmark2]: Bowen
suggestive of polycystic ovary syndrome. Your assessment would be highly appreciated.

On 28/08/2004, Ms Browen came complaining of menstrual disturbances, including irregular menstrual          Comment [Benchmark3]: Bowen
cycles together with painful menstruation. However, her examination was unremarkable. She was
diagnosed with idiopathic oligomenorrhoea with primary dysmenorrhea, for which oral contraceptive pills
were prescribed. On 21/09/2005, the patient presented with facial, shoulder and neck acne, which was
deep and inflamed forming cystic pustules; the reason why tetracycline was given orally and locally. Two    Comment [Benchmark4]: and
                                                                                                            therefore
months later, unfortunately, the condition did not improve; and thus she was referred to a dermatologist.

Today, although Ms Browen got married and stopped taking OCP, she reported a difficulty to conceive.        Comment [Benchmark5]: Bowen
Moreover, she suffered from amenorrhoea, obesity and hirsutism. Some laboratory tests were requested.
Regrettably, the test results revealed multiple hormonal disturbances related to PCOS. Consequently, the
patient was instructed to take Climen. Furthermore, I recommended doing a pelvic ultrasound examination
to be discussed with an endocrinologist.

In light of the above, the patient s being referred for further management. Should you have any queries,    Comment [Benchmark6]: is
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor

                                  range and accuracy.
                              2. Be careful with spelling.
                              3. Always proofread the letter after finishing
